'''Mile Ilić''' ({{Lang-sr-Cyrl|Миле Илић}}; born 2 June 1984) is a Serbian [[podcaster]] and former professional [[basketball]] player.

Known in Serbia as '''Jao Mile''' ([[word play]] referencing [[Yao Ming]] and the [[Serbian language|Serbian]] expression for ouch, {{Wikt-lang|sh|jao}}), the 2.15-metre-tall (7'1") [[Center (basketball)|center]] won two [[Adriatic League]] championships with [[KK FMP (1991–2011)|KK FMP]]. Additionally, he played with the [[New Jersey Nets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) during the [[2006-07 NBA season|2006–07]] season, having been [[2005 NBA draft|drafted one year earlier]] as the 43rd overall pick.

==Early life and career==
Born to a [[Serbs of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Serb]] family in [[Tuzla]], [[Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina|SR Bosnia and Herzegovina]], [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia|SFR Yugoslavia]] due to it being the nearest town with a maternity ward, young Mile was raised in a [[Lopare]] area settlement of {{ill|Priboj (Lopare)|sr|lt=Priboj}} together with two older siblings, including sister {{ill|Slavica Ilić|it|lt=Slavica}} (born 1973) who would soon begin pursuing basketball with the [[ŽKK Jedinstvo Tuzla|Jedinstvo Aida]] youth squads and eventually grow to 193 cm in height.<ref name="Mondo">{{cite news|last=Lalović|first=Nikola|url=https://mondo.rs/Sport/Kosarka/a1676761/Mile-Ilic-intervju-FMP-Crvena-zvezda-NBA-Svetislav-Pesic-i-Milos-Teodosic.html|title=Sa Pešićem je smešno dok tebe ne nagazi! Mile Ilić za MONDO: Teo je uvek bio van sistema|agency=Mondo.rs|date=22 August 2022|access-date=25 August 2022}}</ref><ref name="SportKlub">{{cite news|last=Spasojević Radojević|first=Nina|url=https://sportklub.rs/blog/blog-ostalo/slavica-i-mile-sestra-i-brat-za-velika-dela/|title=Slavica i Mile, sestra i brat za velika dela|agency=[[SportKlub]]|date=18 August 2021|access-date=25 August 2022}}</ref>

After coming up through the Jedinstvo Aida youth system for years, in 1990, youngster Mile's sixteen-year-old sister Slavica Ilić made the team's full squad as replacement at [[center (basketball)|center]] for celebrated future [[FIBA Hall of Fame member|FIBA Hall of Famer]] [[Razija Mujanović]] who had just transferred abroad to play with [[CB Godella]] in [[Spain]].<ref name="SportKlub"/>

With the outbreak of the [[Bosnian War]] in spring 1992, eighteen-year-old Slavica fled the armed conflict area for [[Belgrade]], [[Republic of Serbia (1992–2006)|Serbia]] where she resumed playing professionally, finding a spot on the [[ŽKK Partizan]] roster quickly. Several months later, during summer 1992, her younger eight-year-old brother Mile, who had just finished the first grade of elementary school, was sent by their parents to join her, while the parents and the middle brother stayed behind in their Serb majority home village that had by this time become the scene of fierce shelling by the Muslim forces from the neighbouring hillside settlement of [[Teočak]].<ref name="RTS-podcast">{{cite news|last=Pejović |first=Dragana|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ibz0mHcAn74|title=Bermudski trougao podcast (S2 09): Mile Ilić 'Jao Mile'|agency=[[Radio Television of Serbia]]|date=13 November 2022|access-date=9 December 2022}}</ref> Their father soon joined the armed conflict, fighting as part of the [[Army of Republika Srpska|Republika Srpska Army]] (VRS).<ref name="SportKlub"/> Meanwhile, in Belgrade, joining his eighteen-year-old professional basketball player sister, eight-year-old child Mile, by his own admission in interviews decades later, initially spent majority of his day riding the [[GSP Belgrade|city's public transit]] while waiting for his sister to finish her daily basketball practices.<ref name="RTS-podcast"/> In September 1992, he resumed his schooling, starting second grade at a primary school in Belgrade.<ref name="RTS-podcast"/> However, being cared and provided for by his teenage sister only, without any parental supervision, soon proved untenable and, following a disciplinary incident at school, a decision was made for him to return to his parents in the war zone.<ref name="RTS-podcast"/> The youngster spent the following year and a half attending school in makeshift facilities in his village, before going back to Belgrade in 1994 to rejoin his sister.<ref name="RTS-podcast"/>

Upon returning to Belgrade, encouraged by his sister Slavica, the tall ten-year-old began practicing basketball by enrolling in [[KK Partizan]]'s youth categories coached by [[Aleksandar Bućan]].<ref name="SportKlub"/> Living with his older sister in a [[Konjarnik]] neighbourhood apartment provided for by her basketball salary, in addition to attending primary school, pre-teen Mile bussed to Partizan youth team practices at the 20th October Elementary School gym facilities on the other side of Belgrade in [[Blokovi|Blok 70]].<ref name="SportKlub"/>

By 1996, Slavica Ilić secured a transfer abroad to [[France]] with [[Stade Clermontois BF]] and twelve-year-old Mile rejoined their parents by moving back to Bosnia where the war had ended in the meantime. Still in primary school, he continued pursuing basketball, this time within the KK Rudar Ugljevik youth categories.<ref name="SportKlub"/>

Though now part of a small provincial club well off the radar for most basketball [[Scout (sport)|scouts]], teenage Ilić kept drawing attention due to his exceptional height and, by 1999, he was scouted by [[KK Hemofarm]]'s head coach [[Željko Lukajić]] who facilitated the fifteen-year-old's tryout at the [[Vršac]] club's youth system. Following the late summer 1999 tryout, during which Hemofarm's youth team head coach [[Petar Rodić]] reportedly liked teenage Ilić's skills, the youngster still did not get placed on the team due to the club's 1999-00 youth squad already being completed. Instead, he returned to [[Ugljevik]] where he even enrolled in a local high school. Some ten days later, however, the team created a roster spot for him and the tall teenager joined KK Hemofarm, a club financed by the [[Hemofarm a.d.|state-owned pharmaceutical company of the same name]] led by CEO {{ill|Miodrag Babić|sr}}.

Coached by Rodić, teenage Ilić played for the KK Hemofarm youth team alongside fellow youngsters [[Darko Miličić]], [[Miljan Pupović]], [[Nenad Mišanović]], [[Vukašin Aleksić]], Marko Kolarić, Nikola Tutuš, etc.

==Playing career==

===FMP===
After three seasons in KK Hemofarm's youth system, seeing his opportunities of entering the club's first team limited, Ilić decided to unilaterally leave Vršac during summer 2002 and transfer to [[YUBA League]] rivals [[KK FMP (1991–2011)|FMP]]. The legal basis he took advantage of for doing so was an unmet clause in his [[stipend]]-based contract at Hemofarm that stipulated the club's obligation to provide the youth player with a professional contract by the time he turns eighteen years of age.

Arriving in [[Železnik]], to a club run by club president and owner [[Nebojša Čović]] and sporting director [[Ratko Radovanović]], eighteen-year-old Ilić thus started his first team, full squad career.

In the [[2005 NBA draft]] he was drafted by the [[New Jersey Nets]] as a 43rd overall pick.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/history/draft/2005-draft/ NBA Draft history: 2005 Draft]</ref>

=== New Jersey Nets ===
Having been drafted one year earlier in 2005, Ilić signed for the Nets on 13 September 2006 once a roster spot opened due to [[Zoran Planinić]] leaving the club. Initially, twenty-two-year-old Ilić was brought in as a foreseeable future backup for countryman [[Nenad Krstić]] with the Nets' general manager [[Ed Stefanski]] singling out Ilić's lateral movement, pick-and-roll, and defensive help as well as his overall adaptation to the speed of the NBA game as the areas the NBA rookie needs to improve in.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/espn/print?id=2586292 Nets sign Serb center Ilic, '05 second-round pick]</ref>

On 26 February 2007 the Nets assigned him to the [[Colorado 14ers]], their [[NBA Development League]] affiliate.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/nets/news/All_Access_Online_NETS_ASSIGN_ILIC_TO_14ERS.html NETS ASSIGN MILE ILIC TO COLORADO 14ers OF D-LEAGUE]</ref> Ilić thus became the first player that the Nets assigned to the D-League since instituting affiliate teams (prior to the [[2005–06 NBA season]]). Playing for the 14ers based out of [[Broomfield, Colorado]], his Development League [[2006–07 NBA Development League season|season]] ended early due to an [[ankle]] joint injury in early April 2007. The injury would end up having a major impact on his basketball career in subsequent years.

On 29 October 2007 he was traded by the Nets to [[New Orleans Hornets]] along with [[Bernard Robinson (basketball)|Bernard Robinson]] for [[David Wesley]] (both Ilić and Robinson were immediately waived by the Hornets).<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20071030040827/http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/Hornets_Complete_Deal_With_Net-241093-31.html HORNETS: Hornets Complete Deal With Nets]</ref>

=== Return to Europe ===
After getting waived in the NBA, Ilić returned to Europe and signed with [[Lokomotiv Rostov]] on 26 November 2007.<ref>[http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_KNce8jInH7Qj1EsyH5rjn2.teamID_4661.compID_BYg5Rb55Jw-G5I3MZ6JB01.season_2008.roundID_5872.playerID_46390.coid_Vfe6g8StJowiz8NyA5As,3.articleMode_on.html Ilic, Harrington join Rostov, FIBA November 26, 2007]</ref> However, he never managed to play for the Russian club due to the effects of the nagging ankle injury he had picked up in the United States and then exacerbated at the [[EuroBasket 2007]] training camp with Serbia national team.<ref>[http://www.svevesti.com/a2114-ko%C5%A1arka-mile-ili%C4%87-nije-potpisao-za-lokomotivu Košarka: Mile Ilić nije potpisao za Lokomotivu] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160216012051/http://www.svevesti.com/a2114-ko%C5%A1arka-mile-ili%C4%87-nije-potpisao-za-lokomotivu |date=2016-02-16 }} {{in lang|sr}}</ref><ref name="jaomile-aug2022"/> Instead, the center went back home to Serbia in order to further rehab his ankle.

====Spain====
On 24 February 2008, midway through the 2007–08 season, Ilić signed with the Spanish [[Asociación de Clubs de Baloncesto|ACB]] league club [[CB Bilbao Berri]].<ref>[http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=46887 El pivot serbio Mile Illic llega a un acuerdo con iurbentia Bilbao Basket] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110525145612/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=46887 |date=2011-05-25 }} {{in lang|es}}</ref> Hampered by the recovery process from the ankle injury, he only appeared in 10 games for the club, averaging 5.6 points and 4.1 rebounds per game.

On 28 July 2008, Ilić signed with [[CB Sevilla]] for the 2008–09 season.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20160215032830/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/34196/cajasol-adds-size-with-mile-ilic Cajasol adds size with Mile Ilic]</ref> Playing on a squad with compatriot [[Duško Savanović]] under head coach [[Pedro Martínez (basketball)|Pedro Martínez]], Ilić's not-fully-healed ankle injury got exacerbated again and he started missing games again. On 27 March 2009, he parted ways with Sevilla after averaging only 2 points and 2 rebounds per game.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/75799/cajasol-cut-mile-ilic.html Cajasol cut Mile Ilic]</ref>

The 2009–10 season began with Ilić without a club as teams shied away from acquiring the tall center due to concerns over his re-occurring ankle injury.

==== Seasons in Serbia ====
After ten months away from competitive basketball, Ilić found a club in March 2010, signing for the remainder of the season with [[KK Metalac Valjevo|Metalac Valjevo]] that decided to acquire him after qualifying for the Superleague stage of their [[2009–10 Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian Basketball League]] campaign.<ref>[http://kosarka.rs/main.asp?dir=news&newsid=2904 Mile Ilić debituje za Metalac] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160215220610/http://kosarka.rs/main.asp?dir=news&newsid=2904 |date=2016-02-15 }} {{in lang|sr}}</ref>

For the 2010–11 season he returned to FMP.<ref>[http://www.pressonline.rs/sport/kosarka/136036/jao-mile-predvodi-fmp.html Jao Mile predvodi FMP] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211211053153/http://www.pressonline.rs/sport/kosarka/136036/jao-mile-predvodi-fmp.html |date=2021-12-11 }} {{in lang|sr}}</ref>

The 2011–12 season he played with [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]]. In March 2013, signed with [[KK Vojvodina Srbijagas|Vojvodina Srbijagas]] for the [[2012–13 Basketball League of Serbia|2012–13 Serbian Superleague]] season.<ref>{{cite web| title =Mile Ilić u Vojvodini (Serbian) | publisher = Novosti.rs | date = March 26, 2013 | url =http://www.novosti.rs/vesti/sport.295.html:426199-Mile-Ilic-u-Vojvodini }}</ref>

=== Seasons in the Middle East and stints in Georgia and Lithuania ===
In October 2013, Ilić signed with [[Mahram Tehran BC]] of the [[Iranian Basketball Super League|Iranian Super League]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/world/asia/64336/mahram-tehran-adds-size-with-mile-ilic.html Mahram Tehran adds size with Mile Ilic]</ref> In January 2014, he left Tehran and signed with [[BC MIA Academy|MIA Academy]] of the [[Georgian Super Liga]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=MIA Academy lands Mile Ilic|url=http://basketball.eurobasket.com/Georgia/news/347523|access-date=23 January 2014|newspaper=Eurobasket.com|date=10 January 2014}}</ref>

In 2015, Ilić played for Qatar Sports Club of the [[Qatari Basketball League|Qatari League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Qatar SC bounce back to beat Arabi |url=https://www.menafn.com/qn_news_story_s.aspx?storyid=1094211462&title=Qatar-SC-bounce-back-to-beat-Arabi&src=RSS |website=menafn.com |access-date=13 July 2019}}</ref> On 17 October 2015 he signed with the Lithuanian club [[BC Lietkabelis|Lietkabelis Panevėžys]].<ref>{{cite news|title="Lietkabelio" marškinėlius apsivilks NBA duonos ragavęs serbas|url=http://www.basketnews.lt/news-90053-lietkabelio-marskinelius-apsivilks-nba-duonos-ragaves-serbas.html#.VrtlXh7CqnN|access-date=10 February 2016|work=basketnews.lt|date=17 October 2015|language=lt}}</ref>

In September 2016, Ilić signed with Nuwaidrat of the [[Bahraini Premier League (basketball)|Bahraini Premier League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Mile Ilic replaces Jasmin Perkovic in Nuwaidrat !!|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/Bahrain/news/464250/Mile-Ilic-replaces-Jasmin-Perkovic-in-Nuwaidrat-!!|access-date=27 September 2016|work=Eurobasket.com|date=27 September 2016}}</ref> At the end of March 2017, Ilić signed with [[Tadamon Zouk]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=التضامن يضمّ عملاقاً بطول 216 سنتمتراً|url=http://www.arabasket.com/2017/03/28/tadamon-adds-mile-ilic/|date=28 March 2017|access-date=4 April 2017|archive-date=6 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170406020111/http://www.arabasket.com/2017/03/28/tadamon-adds-mile-ilic/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In July 2017, he returned to Nuwaidrat.<ref>[http://www.eurobasket.com/Serbia/news/495547/Nuwaidrat-welcomes-back-Ilic Nuwaidrat welcomes back Ilic]</ref> In September 2018, Ilić signed for a Bahraini club Al Itihad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mile Ilić svoju 17. profesionalnu sezonu počinje u Al Itihadu |url=http://basketballsphere.com/mile-ilic-svoju-17-profesionalnu-sezonu-pocinje-u-al-itihadu/ |website=basketballsphere.com |access-date=13 July 2019 |archive-date=13 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190713131133/http://basketballsphere.com/mile-ilic-svoju-17-profesionalnu-sezonu-pocinje-u-al-itihadu/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In summer 2019, Ilić played for Al Seeb of the [[Oman Basketball League|Oman League]]. In July 2019, he signed for a Bahraini club Al-Ahli.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mile Ilic (ex As Seeb) joins Al-Ahli |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Bahrain/news/585265/Mile-Ilic-(ex-As-Seeb)-joins-Al-Ahli |website=asia-basket.com/ |access-date=13 July 2019}}</ref> Prior to the 2019–20 season, Ilić signed for Baniyas of the [[UAE National Basketball League|UAE National League]].

==National team==
During late August 2003, nineteen-year-old Ilić represented Serbia-Montenegro at the [[2003 Summer Universiade]] in [[Daegu]], [[South Korea]] as part of the country's [[Serbian men's university basketball team|university basketball team]].<ref name="jaomile-aug2022">{{cite news|last=Lalović|first=Nikola|url=https://mondo.rs/Sport/Kosarka/a1675483/Mile-Ilic-MONDO-intervju-o-reprezentaciji-Srbije-povredi-i-Moki-Slavnicu.html|title=Požurio sam iz Amerike u reprezentaciju, bila je to ludost! Mile Ilić za MONDO: Posle toga sam bio 13. prase|agency=Mondo.rs|date=16 August 2022|access-date=17 August 2022}}</ref> The makeshift squad consisting of ten FMP players plus Milan Bralović and [[Marko Marinović]] from [[KK Borac Čačak|Borac Čačak]] was put together by FMP's head coach [[Vlade Đurović]] on a short notice.<ref name="jaomile-aug2022"/> Following an arduous 36-hour journey from Belgrade via [[London]], [[Hong Kong]], [[Taipei]], and [[Seoul]], the team arrived in Daegu less than 12 hours before its opening game, a hard-fought win versus [[Chinese Taipei at the Universiade|Chinese Taipei]].<ref name="jaomile-aug2022"/> Serbia-Montenegro ended up [[Basketball at the 2003 Summer Universiade|winning gold]].

===Full squad===
====2006 FIBA World Championship====
In summer 2006, fresh off winning the [[2005–06 ABA Goodyear League|Adriatic League]] title with FMP, Ilić was called up for national team duty by head coach [[Dragan Šakota]] as part of [[Serbia and Montenegro men's national basketball team|Serbia and Montenegro]]'s selection process for the upcoming [[2006 FIBA World Championship]] in [[Japan]]. The center ended up making the [[2006 FIBA World Championship squads#Serbia and Montenegro|12-man roster]] taken to the tournament where he played as backup to [[Darko Miličić]].

One year later, Ilić was called up by the new head coach [[Zoran Slavnić|Moka Slavnić]] to the training camp for [[EuroBasket 2007]].<ref name="jaomile-aug2022"/> Carrying an ankle injury from his time in the U.S., hesitant Ilić still showed up on the insistence of head coach Slavnić who reportedly called the player personally on multiple occasions, convincing him eventually.<ref name="jaomile-aug2022"/> At the training camp, Ilić exacerbated his ankle injury and in the end did not make the [[FIBA EuroBasket 2007 squads#Serbia|12-man roster]], with Slavnić picking Miličić and [[Dragan Labović]] for center spots.<ref name="jaomile-aug2022"/> Together with [[Aleksandar Rašić]], Ilić was among the last two players cut from the squad in late August 2007, right before the start of the championship.<ref>{{cite news|last=Čačija|first=Željko|url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2007&mm=08&dd=26&nav_id=260805|title=Bez Ilića i Rašića na EP u Španiji|publisher=[[Politika]]|agency=[[B92]].net|date=26 August 2007|access-date=26 August 2022}}</ref>

At the beginning of summer 2011, after completing a return season with FMP, Ilić was called up by the Serbia national team head coach [[Dušan Ivković]] for the [[EuroBasket 2011]] training camp. Ilić made it to the last 16, this time, before getting cut by Ivković in early August 2011 together with [[Novica Veličković]].<ref>{{cite news|last=|first=|url=https://www.rts.rs/page/sport/sr/litvanija_2011/story/1698/orlovi/935252/duda-se-zahvalio-ilicu.html?tts=yes|title=Duda se zahvalio Iliću|agency=[[Radio Television of Serbia|RTS]].net|date=4 August 2011|access-date=26 August 2022}}</ref>
